items.title: Putter Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 27, 2024
items.q: Because I like him so much, he was such a great guy. ... So anyway Smokey is a friend of Beck.

ctx.x: Well I’ll mark it over here. Your list of studio work includes everyone from Sonny & Cher to Beck if this list is correct. When was the last — do you remember first of all the last studio date, like showing up to play a part? When was the most recent one for you?

Well the thing with Beck was last year but that was a total fluke. I’m not in that business anymore at all, it was a total fluke. There was a country western swing player, guitar player, named Smokey Hormel and we met in New York, actually New Jersey, and I began going to see his gig in Red Hook. And I enjoyed it very much. And these guys were really good country & western players, and I mean really good you know, really good. And there’s a swinging bunch of guys you know. And I mean I’m not that kind of a player…

You know nice, fun. And the producer goes, “Can you play it — make it a little simpler?” I said, “Oh okay.” So [scats]. He says, “Can you make it a little simpler?” [scats] He said, “Well can you make it a little simpler?” So I go to like the nastiest, dirtiest commercial and I go [scats]. He goes, “Yeah, that’s it.” And at that moment I decided this is not why I became a musician. This is not why I became a musician. And I just simply stopped hustling those kind of gigs and within three months I was totally out.…
